questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is the Internet?

options.A: A single computer owned by a government
options.B: A worldwide network of interconnected computer networks that communicate using the TCP/IP protocol suite
options.C: A software application used to browse web pages
options.D: A type of search engine

questions.explanation: The Internet is a worldwide network of interconnected computer networks that communicate using the TCP/IP protocol suite.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What does the word 'Internet' mean?

options.A: Internal network
options.B: Interconnected network of networks
options.C: International television
options.D: Instant network

questions.explanation: The word Internet refers to an interconnected network of networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: Is the Internet a single computer network?

options.A: Yes, it is one centrally controlled network
options.B: No, it is a global system made up of many independently operated networks connected through common protocols
options.C: Yes, it is owned by a single company
options.D: No, it is only a local area network

questions.explanation: The Internet is not a single network; it is a global system of many independently operated networks connected through common protocols.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Internet?

options.A: To manufacture computers
options.B: To exchange information and provide communication and online services across the world
options.C: To store files only on local devices
options.D: To replace all telephones

questions.explanation: The main purpose of the Internet is to exchange information and provide communication and online services across the world.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: Which protocol suite is fundamental to Internet communication?

options.A: FTP only
options.B: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol)
options.C: SMTP only
options.D: HTML

questions.explanation: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the fundamental protocol suite for Internet communication.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is a protocol in computer networking?

options.A: A physical cable used to connect computers
options.B: A set of rules that governs how devices communicate and exchange data
options.C: A type of computer virus
options.D: A web browser feature

questions.explanation: A protocol is a set of rules that governs how devices communicate and exchange data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: Who is commonly called the father of the Internet?

options.A: Tim Berners-Lee
options.B: Vinton G. Cerf and Robert E. Kahn
options.C: Bill Gates
options.D: Steve Jobs

questions.explanation: Vinton G. Cerf and Robert E. Kahn are widely recognised for developing TCP/IP; the Internet's development involved many contributors.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What was ARPANET?

options.A: A modern search engine
options.B: An early packet-switching computer network funded by the United States Advanced Research Projects Agency
options.C: A web browser developed by CERN
options.D: A type of Wi-Fi standard

questions.explanation: ARPANET was an early packet-switching computer network funded by the United States Advanced Research Projects Agency; it became an important precursor to the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: In which year did ARPANET begin operating?
questions.explanation: ARPANET began operating in 1969.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: When was TCP/IP adopted by ARPANET as its standard networking protocol?

options.A: 1 January 1983
options.B: 1 January 1969
options.C: 26 January 1950
options.D: 1 January 1991

questions.explanation: TCP/IP was adopted by ARPANET on 1 January 1983, a key milestone in the development of the modern Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web?

options.A: Vinton Cerf
options.B: Tim Berners-Lee
options.C: Robert Kahn
options.D: Bill Gates

questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web while working at CERN.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: In which year was the World Wide Web proposed?
questions.explanation: The World Wide Web was proposed in 1989.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: When did the Web become publicly available?
questions.explanation: The Web became publicly available in 1991.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: Are the Internet and the World Wide Web the same?

options.A: Yes, they are identical
options.B: No, the Internet is the underlying global network infrastructure; the Web is one service that operates over it
options.C: Yes, both are search engines
options.D: No, the Web is a protocol and the Internet is a browser

questions.explanation: The Internet is the underlying global network infrastructure; the Web is one service that operates over it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: Name some Internet services other than the Web.

options.A: Email, file transfer, instant messaging, voice/video calls, online gaming, remote access and streaming
options.B: Only email
options.C: Only file transfer
options.D: Only online gaming

questions.explanation: Internet services other than the Web include email, file transfer, instant messaging, voice/video calls, online gaming, remote access and streaming.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is an Internet Service Provider (ISP)?

options.A: A company that manufactures web browsers
options.B: An organisation that provides users or organisations with access to the Internet
options.C: A type of IP address
options.D: A search engine

questions.explanation: An ISP is an organisation that provides users or organisations with access to the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: Give examples of Internet access technologies.

options.A: Fibre broadband, cable, DSL, mobile networks, fixed wireless and satellite connections
options.B: Only dial-up
options.C: Only satellite
options.D: Only cable

questions.explanation: Internet access technologies include fibre broadband, cable, DSL, mobile networks, fixed wireless and satellite connections.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is bandwidth?

options.A: The physical width of a network cable
options.B: The maximum data-transfer capacity of a network connection, usually measured in bits per second
options.C: The time taken for data to travel
options.D: The number of devices connected to a network

questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the maximum data-transfer capacity of a network connection, usually measured in bits per second.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is data transfer rate?

options.A: The amount of data transmitted per unit of time, commonly expressed in bit/s, Kbit/s, Mbit/s or Gbit/s
options.B: The total storage capacity of a hard disk
options.C: The number of users on a network
options.D: The time taken to boot a computer

questions.explanation: Data transfer rate is the amount of data transmitted per unit of time, commonly expressed in bit/s, Kbit/s, Mbit/s or Gbit/s.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is latency?

options.A: The time taken for data to travel from a source to a destination and for a response to return
options.B: The maximum data-transfer capacity of a connection
options.C: The amount of data stored on a server
options.D: The number of packets lost in a network

questions.explanation: Latency is the time taken for data to travel from a source to a destination and for a response to return.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is a packet?

options.A: A small unit of data into which information is divided for transmission across a packet-switched network
options.B: A physical connector used in networking
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A software license

questions.explanation: A packet is a small unit of data into which information is divided for transmission across a packet-switched network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is packet switching?

options.A: A method of communication in which data is divided into packets that can travel through a network and are reassembled at the destination
options.B: A method of connecting computers using a single cable
options.C: A way of storing files on a hard disk
options.D: A type of web hosting

questions.explanation: Packet switching is a method of communication in which data is divided into packets that can travel through a network and are reassembled at the destination.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is an IP address?

options.A: A human-readable name such as example.com
options.B: A numerical address used to identify an interface or device on an IP network and help route data to it
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A protocol used for email

questions.explanation: An IP address is a numerical address used to identify an interface or device on an IP network and help route data to it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What are the two major versions of IP?

options.A: IPv1 and IPv2
options.B: IPv4 and IPv6
options.C: IPv3 and IPv5
options.D: IPv0 and IPv9

questions.explanation: The two major versions of IP are IPv4 and IPv6.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?

options.A: 32 bits
options.B: 64 bits
options.C: 128 bits
options.D: 16 bits

questions.explanation: An IPv4 address is 32 bits long.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: How many bits are in an IPv6 address?

options.A: 32 bits
options.B: 64 bits
options.C: 128 bits
options.D: 256 bits

questions.explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits long.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is a domain name?

options.A: A numerical address used to identify a device
options.B: A human-readable name, such as example.com, that identifies an Internet resource and can be translated to an IP address through DNS
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: A domain name is a human-readable name, such as example.com, that identifies an Internet resource and can be translated to an IP address through DNS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is DNS?

options.A: The Domain Name System; it translates domain names into IP addresses and provides other naming information
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used for email
options.D: A software application for downloading files

questions.explanation: DNS is the Domain Name System; it translates domain names into IP addresses and provides other naming information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is a server?

options.A: A computer or software system that provides data, resources or services to other computers called clients
options.B: A computer that only requests data from other computers
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A device used to connect to a phone line

questions.explanation: A server is a computer or software system that provides data, resources or services to other computers called clients.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is a client in client-server computing?

options.A: A computer or application that requests services or resources from a server
options.B: A computer that only provides data to other computers
options.C: A type of network cable
options.D: A protocol used for file transfer

questions.explanation: A client is a computer or application that requests services or resources from a server.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is a modem?

options.A: A device that modulates and demodulates signals, enabling communication over a transmission medium
options.B: A device that only routes packets between networks
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: A modem is a device that modulates and demodulates signals, enabling communication over a transmission medium; modem broadband equipment may combine modem and router functions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is a router?

options.A: A networking device that forwards data packets between networks, such as between a home network and the Internet
options.B: A device that only converts digital signals to analog
options.C: A type of web server
options.D: A software application for browsing

questions.explanation: A router is a networking device that forwards data packets between networks, such as between a home network and the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: What is a Wi-Fi network?

options.A: A wireless local area network based on the IEEE 802.11 family of standards
options.B: A wired network using Ethernet cables
options.C: A type of satellite Internet connection
options.D: A protocol used for email

questions.explanation: A Wi-Fi network is a wireless local area network based on the IEEE 802.11 family of standards.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet: Meaning, History and Basic Concepts
questions.question: Does Wi-Fi itself mean Internet access?

options.A: Yes, Wi-Fi always provides Internet access
options.B: No, Wi-Fi connects devices wirelessly to a local network; that network may or may not have an Internet connection
options.C: Yes, Wi-Fi is another name for the Internet
options.D: No, Wi-Fi is a type of modem

questions.explanation: Wi-Fi connects devices wirelessly to a local network; that network may or may not have an Internet connection.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is the World Wide Web (WWW)?

options.A: A system of interlinked information and resources that users access over the Internet, commonly through web browsers
options.B: The same thing as the Internet infrastructure
options.C: A type of computer network cable
options.D: A protocol used for email

questions.explanation: The Web is a system of interlinked information and resources that users access over the Internet, commonly through web browsers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a web page?

options.A: A document or resource on the Web, commonly written in HTML and viewed in a browser
options.B: A collection of related websites
options.C: A type of web server
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: A web page is a document or resource on the Web, commonly written in HTML and viewed in a browser.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a website?

options.A: A single web page only
options.B: A collection of related web pages and resources, generally organised under a common domain name or web address
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: A website is a collection of related web pages and resources, generally organised under a common domain name or web address.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a home page?

options.A: The main or introductory page of a website, often serving as its starting point
options.B: The last page of a website
options.C: A page that only contains links to other websites
options.D: A type of web server

questions.explanation: A home page is the main or introductory page of a website, often serving as its starting point.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a web portal?

options.A: A website that provides a central gateway to information, services or resources from multiple sources
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for downloading files

questions.explanation: A web portal is a website that provides a central gateway to information, services or resources from multiple sources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a web application?

options.A: Software that users access through a web browser or web interface, often communicating with a server
options.B: A type of computer hardware
options.C: A protocol used for email
options.D: A device used to connect to the Internet

questions.explanation: A web application is software that users access through a web browser or web interface, often communicating with a server.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a static website?

options.A: A website whose pages are generally delivered as stored, fixed files, with the same content for different visitors unless the files are changed
options.B: A website that generates content based on user input
options.C: A website that cannot be accessed over the Internet
options.D: A website that only contains images

questions.explanation: A static website's pages are generally delivered as stored, fixed files, with the same content for different visitors unless the files are changed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a dynamic website?

options.A: A website that can generate or customise content in response to user input, data, login status or other conditions
options.B: A website whose pages never change
options.C: A website that only contains text
options.D: A website that cannot use databases

questions.explanation: A dynamic website can generate or customise content in response to user input, data, login status or other conditions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is CSS?

options.A: Cascading Style Sheets, a language used to describe the presentation and layout of web documents
options.B: A protocol used to transfer web resources
options.C: A type of web server
options.D: A programming language used only for databases

questions.explanation: CSS is Cascading Style Sheets, a language used to describe the presentation and layout of web documents.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is JavaScript commonly used for on websites?

options.A: It adds interactivity and dynamic behaviour to web pages and can also be used on servers and in other environments
options.B: It is only used to style web pages
options.C: It is a protocol used to transfer files
options.D: It is a type of web server

questions.explanation: JavaScript adds interactivity and dynamic behaviour to web pages and can also be used on servers and in other environments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is HTTP?

options.A: Hypertext Transfer Protocol, an application-layer protocol used to transfer web resources between clients and servers
options.B: A markup language used to structure web pages
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A domain name system

questions.explanation: HTTP is Hypertext Transfer Protocol, an application-layer protocol used to transfer web resources between clients and servers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is HTTPS?

options.A: HTTP carried over a secure connection using TLS, providing encryption and authentication of the server and integrity protection for data in transit
options.B: A markup language used for web pages
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A protocol used only for email

questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP carried over a secure connection using TLS, providing encryption and authentication of the server and integrity protection for data in transit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Web Consortium (W3C)?

options.A: The World Wide Web Consortium develops standards and guidelines intended to support the long-term growth and interoperability of the Web
options.B: It manufactures web browsers
options.C: It provides Internet access to users
options.D: It registers domain names only

questions.explanation: The World Wide Web Consortium develops standards and guidelines intended to support the long-term growth and interoperability of the Web.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a web host?

options.A: A service or server that stores website files and makes them accessible over a network, typically the Internet
options.B: A software application used to browse web pages
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A type of domain name

questions.explanation: A web host is a service or server that stores website files and makes them accessible over a network, typically the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is web hosting?

options.A: A service that provides storage and server resources so a website or web application can be accessed online
options.B: A software application used to browse web pages
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A type of domain name

questions.explanation: Web hosting is a service that provides storage and server resources so a website or web application can be accessed online.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a web address?

options.A: The address used to locate a resource on the Web, usually expressed as a URL
options.B: A physical location of a server
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A protocol used for email

questions.explanation: A web address is the address used to locate a resource on the Web, usually expressed as a URL.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a web server?

options.A: Software, and the computer running it, that receives web requests and returns web content or other responses
options.B: A software application used to browse web pages
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A type of domain name

questions.explanation: A web server is software, and the computer running it, that receives web requests and returns web content or other responses.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a web client?

options.A: Software, commonly a browser, that sends requests to web servers and displays or uses their responses
options.B: A computer that stores website files
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A type of domain name

questions.explanation: A web client is software, commonly a browser, that sends requests to web servers and displays or uses their responses.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: World Wide Web (WWW)
questions.question: What is a hyperlink?

options.A: A clickable reference that takes a user to another web page, document, location or resource
options.B: A type of web server
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A type of domain name

questions.explanation: A hyperlink is a clickable reference that takes a user to another web page, document, location or resource.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a domain?

options.A: A named area of the Domain Name System, such as example.com, used to identify Internet resources
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A physical server location

questions.explanation: A domain is a named area of the Domain Name System, such as example.com, used to identify Internet resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a top-level domain (TLD)?

options.A: The final label in a domain name, such as .com, .org, .in or .edu
options.B: The first label in a domain name
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: A top-level domain (TLD) is the final label in a domain name, such as .com, .org, .in or .edu.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a country-code top-level domain (ccTLD)?

options.A: A top-level domain assigned to a country or territory, such as .in for India
options.B: A domain used only by companies
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: A country-code top-level domain (ccTLD) is a top-level domain assigned to a country or territory, such as .in for India.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What does .in represent?

options.A: It is the country-code top-level domain for India
options.B: It is a generic top-level domain for international organisations
options.C: It is a type of web browser
options.D: It is a protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: .in is the country-code top-level domain for India.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a subdomain?

options.A: A domain that is part of a larger domain, such as blog.example.com
options.B: The main domain name only
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: A subdomain is a domain that is part of a larger domain, such as blog.example.com.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a domain registrar?

options.A: An organisation accredited or authorised to register domain names in the relevant domain system
options.B: A software application used to browse web pages
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A type of web server

questions.explanation: A domain registrar is an organisation accredited or authorised to register domain names in the relevant domain system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a landing page?

options.A: A web page designed as the destination for a particular campaign, link or user action
options.B: The home page of a website only
options.C: A page that only contains images
options.D: A type of web server

questions.explanation: A landing page is a web page designed as the destination for a particular campaign, link or user action.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a URL slug?

options.A: A human-readable part of a URL path that often identifies a specific page or content item
options.B: A type of domain name
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for browsing

questions.explanation: A URL slug is a human-readable part of a URL path that often identifies a specific page or content item.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a website navigation menu?

options.A: A set of links that helps visitors move between sections or pages of a website
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for downloading files

questions.explanation: A website navigation menu is a set of links that helps visitors move between sections or pages of a website.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a responsive website?

options.A: A website designed to adapt its layout and content to different screen sizes and devices
options.B: A website that loads very quickly
options.C: A website that cannot be viewed on mobile devices
options.D: A website that only uses static content

questions.explanation: A responsive website is designed to adapt its layout and content to different screen sizes and devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a cookie in web browsing?

options.A: A small piece of data stored by a browser for a website, often used for session management, preferences or analytics
options.B: A type of computer virus
options.C: A physical device used to connect to the Internet
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: A cookie is a small piece of data stored by a browser for a website, often used for session management, preferences or analytics.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a browser cache?

options.A: A local store of previously downloaded resources that can help pages load faster and reduce repeated data transfers
options.B: A list of bookmarked websites
options.C: A record of browsing history
options.D: A type of web server

questions.explanation: A browser cache is a local store of previously downloaded resources that can help pages load faster and reduce repeated data transfers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.chapter: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies
questions.question: What is a web session?

options.A: A period of interaction between a user and a website or application, often maintained using a session identifier
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A physical location of a server

questions.explanation: A web session is a period of interaction between a user and a website or application, often maintained using a session identifier.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.topic: Websites, Web Pages and Web Technologies

questions.question: What does HTTP status code 500 mean?

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers

options.B: It displays bookmarks only

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is a browser tab?

options.A: A separate page or browsing context within the same browser window
options.B: A type of bookmark
options.C: A software extension
options.D: A saved password

questions.explanation: A browser tab is a separate page or browsing context within the same browser window.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is a bookmark or favourite?

options.A: A saved link that allows a user to return to a web page quickly
options.B: A type of browser extension
options.C: A record of all visited pages
options.D: A private browsing window

questions.explanation: A bookmark or favourite is a saved link that allows a user to return to a web page quickly.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is browsing history?

options.A: A record of websites or pages visited by the browser, subject to browser settings and deletion
options.B: A list of saved bookmarks
options.C: A list of installed extensions
options.D: A record of downloaded files only

questions.explanation: Browsing history is a record of websites or pages visited by the browser, subject to browser settings and deletion.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is private or incognito browsing?

options.A: A browsing mode that limits what the browser saves locally after the private session, such as history and cookies; it does not make the user anonymous to websites, employers, schools or Internet providers
options.B: A mode that hides the user's IP address completely
options.C: A mode that blocks all malware
options.D: A mode that encrypts all web traffic

questions.explanation: Private or incognito browsing limits what the browser saves locally after the private session, such as history and cookies; it does not make the user anonymous to websites, employers, schools or Internet providers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: Does incognito mode hide a user's IP address?

options.A: No, private browsing does not by itself hide the user's IP address or provide anonymity
options.B: Yes, it hides the IP address completely
options.C: Yes, it routes traffic through a VPN automatically
options.D: Yes, it encrypts all traffic

questions.explanation: Private browsing does not by itself hide the user's IP address or provide anonymity.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is a browser extension or add-on?

options.A: A small software component that adds or modifies browser functionality
options.B: A type of web server
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A physical device attached to a computer

questions.explanation: A browser extension or add-on is a small software component that adds or modifies browser functionality.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is a browser plug-in?

options.A: A software component historically used to add capabilities to browsers; many older plug-in systems have been discontinued or restricted
options.B: A type of web server
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A hardware device used to connect to the Internet

questions.explanation: A browser plug-in is a software component historically used to add capabilities to browsers; many older plug-in systems have been discontinued or restricted.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is a pop-up window?

options.A: A separate or overlaid browser window or panel opened by a website or browser action
options.B: A type of browser extension
options.C: A saved bookmark
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: A pop-up window is a separate or overlaid browser window or panel opened by a website or browser action.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is a pop-up blocker?

options.A: A browser feature that prevents or limits unwanted pop-up windows
options.B: A type of web server
options.C: A software application for downloading files
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: A pop-up blocker is a browser feature that prevents or limits unwanted pop-up windows.

questions.chapter: Web Browsers

options.A: A feature or tool that tracks and manages files being downloaded

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is the refresh or reload button used for?

options.A: It requests the current page or resource again
options.B: It closes the current tab

options.D: It saves the current page

questions.explanation: The refresh or reload button requests the current page or resource again.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What does the browser Back button do?

options.A: It returns to the previous page in the current tab's browsing history
options.B: It moves to the next page in the tab's history
options.C: It opens the home page
options.D: It closes the current tab

questions.explanation: The Back button returns to the previous page in the current tab's browsing history.

questions.question: What does the Forward button do?

options.A: It moves to the next page in the tab's history when one is available
options.B: It returns to the previous page
options.C: It opens the home page
options.D: It refreshes the current page

questions.explanation: The Forward button moves to the next page in the tab's history when one is available.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What does the Home button do?

options.A: It opens the home page configured in the browser
options.B: It closes the current tab
options.C: It opens a new browser window
options.D: It saves the current page

questions.explanation: The Home button opens the home page configured in the browser.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is a browser's default search engine?

options.A: The search service the browser uses when a user enters a search query in the address bar or search box
options.B: The first bookmark saved in the browser
options.C: The home page configured in the browser
options.D: The most visited website in history

questions.explanation: A browser's default search engine is the search service the browser uses when a user enters a search query in the address bar or search box.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.question: What is a browser profile?

options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A saved password only

questions.explanation: A browser profile is a separate set of browser settings and data, which may include bookmarks, history, extensions and sign-in information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Web Browsers
questions.question: What is browser synchronisation?

options.C: A feature that hides the user's IP address
options.D: A feature that encrypts all web traffic

questions.explanation: Browser synchronisation is a feature that can sync selected browser data, such as bookmarks and passwords, across devices through an account.

options.C: Updates are only needed to add bookmarks
options.D: Updates are only needed to clear browsing history

questions.explanation: Browser updates fix security vulnerabilities, improve stability and performance, and add or maintain features and standards support.

options.D: A warning that a download has completed

questions.explanation: A browser certificate warning indicates that the browser cannot establish the expected secure identity or trust of a website certificate; users should not ignore it without checking.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is a search engine?

options.A: An online service that discovers, indexes and retrieves information from the Web in response to a user's query
options.B: A software application used to browse web pages
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A type of web server

questions.explanation: A search engine is an online service that discovers, indexes and retrieves information from the Web in response to a user's query.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: Name popular search engines.

options.A: Google Search, Microsoft Bing, Yahoo Search, DuckDuckGo and Baidu
options.B: Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox and Microsoft Edge
options.C: Windows, Linux and macOS
options.D: HTTP, HTTPS and FTP

questions.explanation: Popular search engines include Google Search, Microsoft Bing, Yahoo Search, DuckDuckGo and Baidu.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: Which company operates Google Search?

options.A: Google
options.B: Microsoft
options.C: Yahoo
options.D: Baidu

questions.explanation: Google operates Google Search.

questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: Which company operates Bing?

options.A: Microsoft
options.B: Google
options.C: Yahoo
options.D: Baidu

questions.explanation: Microsoft operates Bing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is a search query?

options.A: The word, phrase or question entered into a search engine to find information
options.B: The page displaying results returned by a search engine
options.C: A structured database of discovered web content
options.D: An automated program that visits web pages

questions.explanation: A search query is the word, phrase or question entered into a search engine to find information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is a search results page (SERP)?

options.A: The page displaying results returned by a search engine for a query
options.B: The word or phrase entered into a search engine
options.C: A structured database of discovered web content
options.D: An automated program that visits web pages

questions.explanation: A search results page (SERP) is the page displaying results returned by a search engine for a query.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is a search engine index?

options.A: A structured database of discovered web content that a search engine can retrieve when responding to queries
options.B: The page displaying results returned by a search engine
options.C: An automated program that visits web pages
options.D: A paid advertisement displayed in search results

questions.explanation: A search engine index is a structured database of discovered web content that a search engine can retrieve when responding to queries.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is web crawling?

options.A: The automated process by which software known as crawlers or bots discover and fetch web pages and links
options.B: The process of analysing and storing information about web pages
options.C: The page displaying results returned by a search engine
options.D: A paid advertisement displayed in search results

questions.explanation: Web crawling is the automated process by which software known as crawlers or bots discover and fetch web pages and links.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is a web crawler or spider?

options.A: An automated program that visits web pages and follows links to discover content for indexing or other purposes
options.B: A structured database of discovered web content
options.C: The page displaying results returned by a search engine
options.D: A paid advertisement displayed in search results

questions.explanation: A web crawler or spider is an automated program that visits web pages and follows links to discover content for indexing or other purposes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is web indexing?

options.A: The process of analysing and storing information about web pages so a search engine can retrieve them
options.B: The automated process by which crawlers discover and fetch web pages
options.C: The page displaying results returned by a search engine
options.D: A paid advertisement displayed in search results

questions.explanation: Web indexing is the process of analysing and storing information about web pages so a search engine can retrieve them.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is an organic search result?

options.A: A non-paid search result selected and ranked by the search engine's systems
options.B: A paid advertisement displayed in or near search results
options.C: A result arranged alphabetically
options.D: A result that is always the most reliable

questions.explanation: An organic search result is a non-paid search result selected and ranked by the search engine's systems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is a sponsored search result?

options.A: A paid advertisement displayed in or near search results
options.B: A non-paid search result selected and ranked by the search engine's systems
options.C: A result arranged alphabetically
options.D: A result that is always the most reliable

questions.explanation: A sponsored search result is a paid advertisement displayed in or near search results.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: Are search-engine results always arranged alphabetically?

options.A: No, search engines generally rank results using many relevance, quality, context and other signals
options.B: Yes, they are always alphabetical
options.C: Yes, they are always by date
options.D: No, they are always random

questions.explanation: Search engines generally rank results using many relevance, quality, context and other signals, not alphabetically.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What are keywords in searching?

options.A: Important words or phrases that describe the information a user wants to find
options.B: Paid advertisements displayed in search results
options.C: The page displaying results returned by a search engine
options.D: An automated program that visits web pages

questions.explanation: Keywords are important words or phrases that describe the information a user wants to find.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What does the minus sign do in many search engines?

options.A: It can exclude results containing a specified term, for example jaguar -car
options.B: It requests an exact phrase match
options.C: It restricts results to a specified file type
options.D: It searches within a particular website

questions.explanation: The minus sign can exclude results containing a specified term, for example jaguar -car.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: How can a user search within a particular website?

options.A: Use the site: operator, for example site:gov.in recruitment
options.B: Use quotation marks around the website name
options.C: Use the filetype: operator
options.D: Use the minus sign before the website name

questions.explanation: The site: operator can be used to search within a particular website, for example site:gov.in recruitment.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What does the filetype: search operator do?

options.A: It can restrict results to a specified file type, such as filetype:pdf
options.B: It searches within a particular website
options.C: It excludes results containing a specified term
options.D: It requests an exact phrase match

questions.explanation: The filetype: operator can restrict results to a specified file type, such as filetype:pdf.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: How can a user search for a specific phrase?

options.A: Place the phrase inside quotation marks, for example "Indian Constitution"
options.B: Use the minus sign before the phrase
options.C: Use the site: operator
options.D: Use the filetype: operator

questions.explanation: Placing a phrase inside quotation marks searches for that specific phrase, for example "Indian Constitution".

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: How can a user search for either of two terms?

options.A: Use OR between the terms in search engines that support the operator
options.B: Use AND between the terms
options.C: Use quotation marks around the terms
options.D: Use the minus sign before the terms

questions.explanation: Using OR between two terms searches for either term in search engines that support the operator.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

options.C: A search feature that finds news articles
options.D: A search feature that locates places and routes

questions.explanation: An image search is a search feature that finds images related to a query.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is a reverse image search?
