options.B: A search feature that finds images related to a text query
options.C: A search feature that finds news articles
options.D: A search feature that locates places and routes

questions.explanation: A reverse image search is a search method that uses an image to find visually similar images or web pages where the image appears.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is a news search?

options.A: A search feature that finds news articles and reports related to a query
options.B: A search feature that finds images related to a query
options.C: A search feature that locates places and routes
options.D: A search method that uses an image to find similar images

questions.explanation: A news search is a search feature that finds news articles and reports related to a query.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is a map search?

options.A: A search feature that locates places, addresses, routes and local businesses
options.B: A search feature that finds images related to a query
options.C: A search feature that finds news articles
options.D: A search method that uses an image to find similar images

questions.explanation: A map search is a search feature that locates places, addresses, routes and local businesses.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: What is safe search?

options.A: A search-engine setting designed to filter or limit explicit or potentially inappropriate content
options.B: A search feature that finds images related to a query
options.C: A search method that uses an image to find similar images
options.D: A search feature that locates places and routes

questions.explanation: Safe search is a search-engine setting designed to filter or limit explicit or potentially inappropriate content.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: Why should search results be verified?

options.A: Search results can contain outdated, inaccurate, biased, sponsored or misleading information
options.B: Search results are always completely accurate
options.C: Search results are always arranged alphabetically
options.D: Search results never contain advertisements

questions.explanation: Search results can contain outdated, inaccurate, biased, sponsored or misleading information, so they should be verified.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: How can the reliability of a website be assessed?

options.A: Check the author or organisation, publication date, evidence, references, purpose, domain context and whether independent reliable sources corroborate the claim
options.B: Check only the domain suffix
options.C: Check only the visual design of the website
options.D: Check only the number of advertisements on the page

questions.explanation: Website reliability can be assessed by checking the author or organisation, publication date, evidence, references, purpose, domain context and whether independent reliable sources corroborate the claim.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: Does a .org domain guarantee that a website is trustworthy?

options.A: No, a domain suffix alone does not guarantee accuracy, credibility or non-profit status
options.B: Yes, .org websites are always trustworthy
options.C: Yes, .org websites are always non-profit
options.D: Yes, .org websites are always government-owned

questions.explanation: A domain suffix alone does not guarantee accuracy, credibility or non-profit status.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Search Engines and Effective Searching
questions.question: Does a .gov.in domain generally identify an Indian government website?

options.A: Yes, .gov.in is used for Indian government entities, but users should still verify the exact address and secure connection
options.B: No, .gov.in is used for private companies
options.C: No, .gov.in is used for non-profit organisations
options.D: Yes, and no further verification is ever needed

questions.explanation: .gov.in is used for Indian government entities, but users should still verify the exact address and secure connection.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is a URL?

options.A: Uniform Resource Locator; it is the address used to identify and locate a resource on a network, commonly on the Web
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for downloading files

questions.explanation: A URL is a Uniform Resource Locator; it is the address used to identify and locate a resource on a network, commonly on the Web.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What are the main parts of a typical URL?

options.A: A scheme or protocol, host or domain, optional port, path, optional query string and optional fragment
options.B: Only the domain name
options.C: Only the path and query string
options.D: Only the scheme and fragment

questions.explanation: A typical URL has a scheme or protocol, host or domain, optional port, path, optional query string and optional fragment.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: In https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, what is the scheme?

options.A: https
options.B: www.example.com
options.C: /news
options.D: ?id=5

questions.explanation: In the URL https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, the scheme is https.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: In https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, what is the host?

options.A: www.example.com
options.B: https
options.C: /news
options.D: #top

questions.explanation: In the URL https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, the host is www.example.com.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: In https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, what is the path?

options.A: /news
options.B: https
options.C: www.example.com
options.D: ?id=5

questions.explanation: In the URL https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, the path is /news.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: In https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, what is the query string?

options.A: ?id=5
options.B: /news
options.C: #top
options.D: https

questions.explanation: In the URL https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, the query string is ?id=5.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: In https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, what is the fragment?

options.A: #top
options.B: ?id=5
options.C: /news
options.D: www.example.com

questions.explanation: In the URL https://www.example.com/news?id=5#top, the fragment is #top.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What does HTTP stand for?

options.A: Hypertext Transfer Protocol
options.B: Hypertext Markup Language
options.C: Hyperlink Text Protocol
options.D: High Transfer Text Protocol

questions.explanation: HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What does HTTPS stand for?

options.A: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure; it is HTTP protected by TLS
options.B: Hypertext Markup Language Secure
options.C: Hyperlink Text Protocol Standard
options.D: High Transfer Text Protocol Secure

questions.explanation: HTTPS stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure; it is HTTP protected by TLS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is the default port commonly used by HTTP?

options.A: TCP port 80
options.B: TCP port 443
options.C: TCP port 21
options.D: TCP port 25

questions.explanation: The default port commonly used by HTTP is TCP port 80.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is the default port commonly used by HTTPS?

options.A: TCP port 443
options.B: TCP port 80
options.C: TCP port 21
options.D: TCP port 25

questions.explanation: The default port commonly used by HTTPS is TCP port 443.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is the host portion of a URL?

options.A: The part identifying the server or host, commonly a domain name or IP address
options.B: The part introduced by ? that carries parameters
options.C: The part introduced by # that identifies a section within a document
options.D: The part that identifies a resource on the host

questions.explanation: The host portion of a URL identifies the server or host, commonly a domain name or IP address.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is a URL path?

options.A: The part of a URL that identifies a resource or location on the host
options.B: The part introduced by ? that carries parameters
options.C: The part introduced by # that identifies a section within a document
options.D: The part identifying the server or host

questions.explanation: A URL path is the part of a URL that identifies a resource or location on the host.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is a query string in a URL?

options.A: A part introduced by ? that carries parameters, often as key-value pairs
options.B: The part introduced by # that identifies a section within a document
options.C: The part identifying the server or host
options.D: The part that identifies a resource on the host

questions.explanation: A query string in a URL is a part introduced by ? that carries parameters, often as key-value pairs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is a URL fragment identifier?

options.A: The part introduced by # that identifies a location or section within a resource or document
options.B: The part introduced by ? that carries parameters
options.C: The part identifying the server or host
options.D: The part that identifies a resource on the host

questions.explanation: A URL fragment identifier is the part introduced by # that identifies a location or section within a resource or document.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is URL encoding?

options.A: A method of representing characters in a URL using percent-encoded bytes, commonly shown as % followed by hexadecimal digits
options.B: A method of encrypting the entire URL
options.C: A method of shortening a URL
options.D: A method of hiding the destination of a URL

questions.explanation: URL encoding is a method of representing characters in a URL using percent-encoded bytes, commonly shown as % followed by hexadecimal digits.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What does the URL character sequence %20 commonly represent?

options.A: A space character in percent-encoded URL data
options.B: A question mark
options.C: A hash symbol
options.D: A forward slash

questions.explanation: The URL character sequence %20 commonly represents a space character in percent-encoded URL data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is a shortened URL?

options.A: A compact link that redirects users to a longer destination URL
options.B: A URL that has been encrypted
options.C: A URL that contains only a domain name
options.D: A URL that is no longer valid

questions.explanation: A shortened URL is a compact link that redirects users to a longer destination URL.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What risk can shortened URLs create?

options.A: They can conceal the destination, so users may be redirected to phishing or malicious sites
options.B: They always expire within one hour
options.C: They cannot be opened in a browser
options.D: They always contain malware

questions.explanation: Shortened URLs can conceal the destination, so users may be redirected to phishing or malicious sites.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is a domain name hierarchy?

options.A: A hierarchical naming structure consisting of labels, such as a top-level domain, second-level domain and optional subdomains
options.B: A list of all URLs on a website
options.C: A method of encrypting domain names
options.D: A type of web browser

questions.explanation: A domain name hierarchy is a hierarchical naming structure consisting of labels, such as a top-level domain, second-level domain and optional subdomains.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: In example.com, what is .com?

options.A: The top-level domain
options.B: The second-level domain
options.C: A subdomain
options.D: The host name

questions.explanation: In example.com, .com is the top-level domain.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: In www.example.com, what is www?

options.A: A subdomain label commonly used for a website host; it is not compulsory
options.B: The top-level domain
options.C: The second-level domain
options.D: A protocol

questions.explanation: In www.example.com, www is a subdomain label commonly used for a website host; it is not compulsory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is the difference between a domain name and a URL?

options.A: A domain name identifies a domain; a URL identifies a particular resource and may include the domain plus protocol, path and other components
options.B: A domain name is always longer than a URL
options.C: A URL is only the domain name
options.D: They are exactly the same thing

questions.explanation: A domain name identifies a domain; a URL identifies a particular resource and may include the domain plus protocol, path and other components.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: What is a secure website certificate used for?

options.A: It helps authenticate the website's identity and enables an encrypted TLS connection when properly validated
options.B: It guarantees that the website content is honest and safe
options.C: It hides the user's IP address
options.D: It blocks all malware on the website

questions.explanation: A secure website certificate helps authenticate the website's identity and enables an encrypted TLS connection when properly validated.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: URLs, Web Addresses and Domain Names
questions.question: Does HTTPS prove that a website's content is honest or safe?

options.A: No, HTTPS protects the connection; it does not guarantee that the website is legitimate, truthful or free of malware
options.B: Yes, HTTPS guarantees the website is safe
options.C: Yes, HTTPS guarantees the website is honest
options.D: Yes, HTTPS guarantees the website is free of malware

questions.explanation: HTTPS protects the connection; it does not guarantee that the website is legitimate, truthful or free of malware.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is a hyperlink?

options.A: A reference embedded in text, an image or another element that users can activate to open another resource or location
options.B: A type of web server
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for downloading files

questions.explanation: A hyperlink is a reference embedded in text, an image or another element that users can activate to open another resource or location.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is anchor text?

options.A: The visible, clickable text of a text hyperlink
options.B: The destination URL of a hyperlink
options.C: A link that points to another page within the same website
options.D: A link that points to a resource on a different website

questions.explanation: Anchor text is the visible, clickable text of a text hyperlink.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is an internal link?

options.A: A hyperlink that points to another page or resource within the same website
options.B: A hyperlink that points to a resource on a different website or domain
options.C: A link that takes the user to a particular section within a page
options.D: A link that opens an email application

questions.explanation: An internal link is a hyperlink that points to another page or resource within the same website.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is an external link?

options.A: A hyperlink that points to a resource on a different website or domain
options.B: A hyperlink that points to another page or resource within the same website
options.C: A link that takes the user to a particular section within a page
options.D: A link that opens an email application

questions.explanation: An external link is a hyperlink that points to a resource on a different website or domain.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is an in-page or anchor link?

options.A: A link that takes the user to a particular section or element within a page, often using a URL fragment
options.B: A link that points to a resource on a different website
options.C: A link that points to another page within the same website
options.D: A link that opens an email application

questions.explanation: An in-page or anchor link takes the user to a particular section or element within a page, often using a URL fragment.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: Can an image act as a hyperlink?

options.A: Yes, an image can be placed inside a link so that selecting it opens the linked destination
options.B: No, only text can be a hyperlink
options.C: Yes, but only if the image is animated
options.D: No, images cannot be clicked

questions.explanation: An image can be placed inside a link so that selecting it opens the linked destination.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is a mailto hyperlink?

options.A: A link that opens a configured email application to compose a message to a specified email address
options.B: A link that downloads a file
options.C: A link that opens a particular section within a page
options.D: A link that points to a resource on a different website

questions.explanation: A mailto hyperlink opens a configured email application to compose a message to a specified email address.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is a download link?

options.A: A hyperlink that opens or downloads a file, depending on the server response and browser behaviour
options.B: A link that opens an email application
options.C: A link that takes the user to a particular section within a page
options.D: A link that points to a resource on a different website

questions.explanation: A download link is a hyperlink that opens or downloads a file, depending on the server response and browser behaviour.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is a broken link?

options.A: A hyperlink whose destination is unavailable or cannot be reached as intended
options.B: A link that opens an email application
options.C: A link that downloads a file
options.D: A link that takes the user to a particular section within a page

questions.explanation: A broken link is a hyperlink whose destination is unavailable or cannot be reached as intended.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is link text accessibility?

options.A: The practice of using clear, meaningful link text so users, including those using assistive technologies, can understand the link's purpose
options.B: The practice of making links as short as possible
options.C: The practice of hiding links from users
options.D: The practice of using only images as links

questions.explanation: Link text accessibility is the practice of using clear, meaningful link text so users, including those using assistive technologies, can understand the link's purpose.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is a breadcrumb trail on a website?

options.A: A navigation aid showing the page's position in the website hierarchy and links to higher-level pages
options.B: A list of all pages on a website
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: A breadcrumb trail is a navigation aid showing the page's position in the website hierarchy and links to higher-level pages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is a redirect?

options.A: A server or client instruction that sends a browser from one URL to another
options.B: A type of hyperlink that opens an email application
options.C: A link that takes the user to a particular section within a page
options.D: A software application for downloading files

questions.explanation: A redirect is a server or client instruction that sends a browser from one URL to another.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is a hyperlink's target?

options.A: The destination resource or browsing context that opens when the link is activated
options.B: The visible text of a hyperlink
options.C: The colour of a hyperlink
options.D: The website where the link is located

questions.explanation: A hyperlink's target is the destination resource or browsing context that opens when the link is activated.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Hyperlinks and Navigation
questions.question: What is the difference between clicking a link and downloading a file?

options.A: A link may open a page or resource in the browser, while downloading saves a copy of a file to the user's device; the result depends on the resource and browser/server settings
options.B: They are exactly the same action
options.C: Downloading always opens a page in the browser
options.D: Clicking a link always saves a file to the device

questions.explanation: A link may open a page or resource in the browser, while downloading saves a copy of a file to the user's device; the result depends on the resource and browser/server settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is downloading?

options.A: The process of receiving data or a file from a remote system, such as a web server, and transferring it to a local device
options.B: The process of sending data or a file from a local device to a remote system
options.C: The process of compressing a file
options.D: The process of extracting a file

questions.explanation: Downloading is the process of receiving data or a file from a remote system, such as a web server, and transferring it to a local device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is uploading?

options.A: The process of sending data or a file from a local device to a remote system, such as a website or cloud service
options.B: The process of receiving data or a file from a remote system
options.C: The process of compressing a file
options.D: The process of extracting a file

questions.explanation: Uploading is the process of sending data or a file from a local device to a remote system, such as a website or cloud service.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is the difference between downloading and uploading?

options.A: Downloading transfers data to the user's device; uploading transfers data from the user's device to a remote system
options.B: Downloading transfers data from the user's device; uploading transfers data to the user's device
options.C: They are exactly the same process
options.D: Downloading only works with images; uploading only works with documents

questions.explanation: Downloading transfers data to the user's device; uploading transfers data from the user's device to a remote system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: Give an example of downloading.

options.A: Saving a PDF application form from a government website to a computer
options.B: Submitting a scanned certificate to an online application portal
options.C: Sending an email to a friend
options.D: Creating a new document in a word processor

questions.explanation: Saving a PDF application form from a government website to a computer is an example of downloading.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: Give an example of uploading.

options.A: Submitting a scanned certificate from a computer to an online application portal
options.B: Saving a PDF application form from a government website to a computer
options.C: Opening a web page in a browser
options.D: Searching for information on a search engine

questions.explanation: Submitting a scanned certificate from a computer to an online application portal is an example of uploading.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: Where are downloaded files commonly stored by default?

options.A: In the device's Downloads folder, unless the user or application has selected another location
options.B: In the Recycle Bin
options.C: In the browser's bookmark list
options.D: In the Documents folder only

questions.explanation: Downloaded files are commonly stored by default in the device's Downloads folder, unless the user or application has selected another location.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: How can a user find a downloaded file in a browser?

options.A: Open the browser's Downloads list or use the Downloads folder in the operating system's file manager
options.B: Open the browser's bookmark list
options.C: Open the browser's history
options.D: Open the browser's settings page

questions.explanation: A user can find a downloaded file by opening the browser's Downloads list or using the Downloads folder in the operating system's file manager.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is a download manager?

options.A: A program or browser feature that organises downloads and may support pause, resume, queueing and progress tracking
options.B: A type of web server
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A saved bookmark

questions.explanation: A download manager is a program or browser feature that organises downloads and may support pause, resume, queueing and progress tracking.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is download speed?

options.A: The rate at which data is received from a remote source, usually measured in bits per second
options.B: The rate at which data is sent from a local device to a remote destination
options.C: The total storage capacity of a hard disk
options.D: The number of files stored in the Downloads folder

questions.explanation: Download speed is the rate at which data is received from a remote source, usually measured in bits per second.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is upload speed?

options.A: The rate at which data is sent from a local device to a remote destination, usually measured in bits per second
options.B: The rate at which data is received from a remote source
options.C: The total storage capacity of a hard disk
options.D: The number of files in the Downloads folder

questions.explanation: Upload speed is the rate at which data is sent from a local device to a remote destination, usually measured in bits per second.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: Why can upload and download speeds differ?

options.A: Internet plans and network technologies may provide asymmetric bandwidth, and actual speeds also depend on congestion, server capacity and other factors
options.B: Upload speed is always faster than download speed
options.C: Download speed is always faster than upload speed
options.D: They never differ on any network

questions.explanation: Internet plans and network technologies may provide asymmetric bandwidth, and actual speeds also depend on congestion, server capacity and other factors.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is a file size?

options.A: The amount of digital storage occupied by a file, commonly measured in bytes and multiples such as KB, MB and GB
options.B: The rate at which data is transferred
options.C: The number of files in a folder
options.D: The time taken to download a file

questions.explanation: File size is the amount of digital storage occupied by a file, commonly measured in bytes and multiples such as KB, MB and GB.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is the difference between bit and byte?

options.A: A bit is a binary digit; a byte is commonly 8 bits. Network speeds are usually expressed in bits per second, while file sizes are commonly expressed in bytes
options.B: A bit is 8 bytes
options.C: A byte is a binary digit
options.D: They are exactly the same unit

questions.explanation: A bit is a binary digit; a byte is commonly 8 bits. Network speeds are usually expressed in bits per second, while file sizes are commonly expressed in bytes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What does Mbps mean?

options.A: Megabits per second, a unit commonly used to express network data-transfer rates
options.B: Megabytes per second
options.C: Millibits per second
options.D: Megabits per minute

questions.explanation: Mbps means Megabits per second, a unit commonly used to express network data-transfer rates.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What does MB/s mean?

options.A: Megabytes per second, a unit of data-transfer rate; 1 MB/s equals 8 Mb/s when using decimal units
options.B: Megabits per second
options.C: Millibits per second
options.D: Megabytes per minute

questions.explanation: MB/s means Megabytes per second, a unit of data-transfer rate; 1 MB/s equals 8 Mb/s when using decimal units.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is a download interruption?

options.A: A break in a file transfer caused by connection loss, server issues, device shutdown or other problems
options.B: A file that has been successfully downloaded
options.C: A type of download manager
options.D: A compressed file

questions.explanation: A download interruption is a break in a file transfer caused by connection loss, server issues, device shutdown or other problems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: Can an interrupted download be resumed?

options.A: Sometimes. Resume support depends on the server, protocol, browser or download manager
options.B: No, an interrupted download can never be resumed
options.C: Yes, an interrupted download can always be resumed
options.D: Only if the file is smaller than 1 MB

questions.explanation: An interrupted download can sometimes be resumed; resume support depends on the server, protocol, browser or download manager.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is a compressed file?

options.A: A file or archive in which data has been encoded to reduce storage size or combine multiple files, such as ZIP or 7z
options.B: A file that has been deleted
options.C: A file that has been uploaded to a website
options.D: A file that has been scanned for malware

questions.explanation: A compressed file is a file or archive in which data has been encoded to reduce storage size or combine multiple files, such as ZIP or 7z.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is a ZIP file?

options.A: A common archive format that can store one or more files and folders, often with compression
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: A ZIP file is a common archive format that can store one or more files and folders, often with compression.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is file extraction?

options.A: The process of unpacking files from a compressed archive into a folder or destination
options.B: The process of compressing files into an archive
options.C: The process of downloading a file from a website
options.D: The process of uploading a file to a website

questions.explanation: File extraction is the process of unpacking files from a compressed archive into a folder or destination.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: Why should downloaded files be scanned or checked?

options.A: Files may contain malware or be disguised as legitimate documents; scanning and checking the source reduces risk
options.B: Downloaded files are always safe
options.C: Scanning is only needed for image files
options.D: Scanning increases the file size

questions.explanation: Downloaded files may contain malware or be disguised as legitimate documents; scanning and checking the source reduces risk.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: Why should file extensions be checked before opening a download?

options.A: The extension helps identify the file type, and unexpected executable extensions may indicate a risky or disguised file
options.B: The extension determines the file's download speed
options.C: The extension determines the file's upload limit
options.D: The extension is only used for images

questions.explanation: The extension helps identify the file type, and unexpected executable extensions may indicate a risky or disguised file.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is a secure download source?

options.A: A source whose identity and legitimacy have been independently verified, such as the official website or trusted distribution channel of the provider
options.B: Any website that offers free downloads
options.C: A website that uses pop-up advertisements
options.D: A shortened URL

questions.explanation: A secure download source is a source whose identity and legitimacy have been independently verified, such as the official website or trusted distribution channel of the provider.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What should a user do before uploading a document to a website?

options.A: Verify the website and its address, confirm the requested file and format, check the file contents, and avoid uploading unnecessary personal information
options.B: Upload the document without checking anything
options.C: Share the document on social media first
options.D: Rename the file to a random name

questions.explanation: Before uploading a document, a user should verify the website and its address, confirm the requested file and format, check the file contents, and avoid uploading unnecessary personal information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is a file upload limit?

options.A: The maximum file size or quantity a website or service permits a user to upload
options.B: The maximum speed at which a file can be downloaded
options.C: The number of files stored in the Downloads folder
options.D: The total storage capacity of a hard disk

questions.explanation: A file upload limit is the maximum file size or quantity a website or service permits a user to upload.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: Why might an upload fail?

options.A: Possible causes include an unstable connection, file-size limit, unsupported format, incorrect permissions, server error or session timeout
options.B: Uploads never fail
options.C: Uploads fail only when the file is too small
options.D: Uploads fail only when the file is an image

questions.explanation: An upload might fail due to an unstable connection, file-size limit, unsupported format, incorrect permissions, server error or session timeout.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is drag and drop upload?

options.A: A method of uploading in which the user drags a file from the device's file manager and drops it into a designated area on a webpage
options.B: A method of downloading a file by dragging it to the desktop
options.C: A method of compressing a file before uploading
options.D: A method of scanning a file for malware

questions.explanation: Drag and drop upload is a method of uploading in which the user drags a file from the device's file manager and drops it into a designated area on a webpage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is cloud storage?

options.A: A service that stores files on remote servers and makes them accessible over a network, subject to account and access permissions
options.B: A type of local hard disk
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: Cloud storage is a service that stores files on remote servers and makes them accessible over a network, subject to account and access permissions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: What is synchronisation in cloud storage?

options.A: The process of keeping selected files or folders consistent across devices or remote storage locations
options.B: The process of compressing files before uploading
options.C: The process of scanning files for malware
options.D: The process of deleting files from the cloud

questions.explanation: Synchronisation in cloud storage is the process of keeping selected files or folders consistent across devices or remote storage locations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Downloads and Uploads
questions.question: Does uploading a file always make it public?

options.A: No, visibility depends on the service's sharing settings, access controls and permissions
options.B: Yes, all uploaded files are public
options.C: Yes, unless the file is a PDF
options.D: No, uploaded files are always private

questions.explanation: Uploading a file does not always make it public; visibility depends on the service's sharing settings, access controls and permissions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is cyber security?

options.A: The practice of protecting systems, networks, devices and data from unauthorised access, attacks, damage or disruption
options.B: The practice of designing websites
options.C: The practice of registering domain names
options.D: The practice of writing HTML code

questions.explanation: Cyber security is the practice of protecting systems, networks, devices and data from unauthorised access, attacks, damage or disruption.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is phishing?

options.A: A fraudulent attempt to trick users into revealing sensitive information or installing malware, often through deceptive emails, messages or websites
options.B: A method of improving website visibility in search results
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A protocol used to transfer files

questions.explanation: Phishing is a fraudulent attempt to trick users into revealing sensitive information or installing malware, often through deceptive emails, messages or websites.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a malicious website?

options.A: A website designed to harm users, steal information, distribute malware or conduct other harmful activity
options.B: A website that loads slowly
options.C: A website with many advertisements
options.D: A website that requires a login

questions.explanation: A malicious website is a website designed to harm users, steal information, distribute malware or conduct other harmful activity.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is malware?

options.A: Malicious software designed to disrupt, damage, spy on or gain unauthorised access to systems or data
options.B: Software used to browse the web
options.C: Software used to create websites
options.D: Software used to compress files

questions.explanation: Malware is malicious software designed to disrupt, damage, spy on or gain unauthorised access to systems or data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a computer virus?

options.A: A type of malware that attaches to a host file or program and replicates when the infected host is executed
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A hardware device used to connect to the Internet

questions.explanation: A computer virus is a type of malware that attaches to a host file or program and replicates when the infected host is executed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a Trojan horse?

options.A: Malware that disguises itself as legitimate or useful software to trick users into running it
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A hardware device used to connect to the Internet

questions.explanation: A Trojan horse is malware that disguises itself as legitimate or useful software to trick users into running it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is ransomware?

options.A: Malware that blocks access to data or systems, commonly by encrypting files, and demands payment for restoration
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: Ransomware is malware that blocks access to data or systems, commonly by encrypting files, and demands payment for restoration.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is spyware?

options.A: Software that secretly monitors activity or collects information without appropriate user awareness or consent
options.B: Software used to browse the web
options.C: Software used to create websites
options.D: Software used to compress files

questions.explanation: Spyware is software that secretly monitors activity or collects information without appropriate user awareness or consent.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a strong password?

options.A: A password that is long, unique and difficult to guess; a password manager can help create and store unique passwords
options.B: A password that uses only your name and birth year
options.C: A password that is the same across all accounts
options.D: A password that is shorter than six characters

questions.explanation: A strong password is long, unique and difficult to guess; a password manager can help create and store unique passwords.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is multi-factor authentication (MFA)?

options.A: An authentication method requiring two or more different categories of evidence, such as something the user knows, has or is
options.B: A method of using the same password on multiple accounts
options.C: A method of storing passwords in a browser
options.D: A method of sharing passwords with trusted contacts

questions.explanation: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is an authentication method requiring two or more different categories of evidence, such as something the user knows, has or is.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: Why should users avoid reusing passwords?

options.A: If one service is breached, attackers may try the same password on other accounts
options.B: Reusing passwords makes logging in slower
options.C: Reusing passwords increases the file download speed
options.D: Reusing passwords is required by most websites

questions.explanation: Users should avoid reusing passwords because if one service is breached, attackers may try the same password on other accounts.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a one-time password (OTP)?

options.A: A temporary authentication code intended for one use or a limited period
options.B: A password that can be used forever
options.C: A password that is shared among all users
options.D: A password that is stored in a browser

questions.explanation: A one-time password (OTP) is a temporary authentication code intended for one use or a limited period.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: Should an OTP be shared with another person who calls or messages?

options.A: No, users should never disclose an OTP to an unverified person; legitimate support staff should not ask for it
options.B: Yes, if the caller claims to be from the bank
options.C: Yes, if the caller is a family member
options.D: Yes, if the message looks official

questions.explanation: Users should never disclose an OTP to an unverified person; legitimate support staff should not ask for it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a digital footprint?

options.A: The trail of information a person leaves through online activities, posts, interactions and data collection
options.B: The amount of storage used by a website
options.C: The number of devices connected to a network
options.D: The speed of an Internet connection

questions.explanation: A digital footprint is the trail of information a person leaves through online activities, posts, interactions and data collection.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is personal data?

options.A: Information relating to an identified or identifiable individual
options.B: Information about the weather
options.C: Information about a website's design
options.D: Information about a computer's hardware

questions.explanation: Personal data is information relating to an identified or identifiable individual.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a privacy setting?

options.A: A control that determines how information, activity or content is collected, used or shared by a service
options.B: A setting that controls the screen brightness
options.C: A setting that controls the download speed
options.D: A setting that controls the browser zoom level

questions.explanation: A privacy setting is a control that determines how information, activity or content is collected, used or shared by a service.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a secure Wi-Fi practice?

options.A: Use a trusted network, enable modern Wi-Fi security such as WPA2 or WPA3, change default router credentials and keep router firmware updated
options.B: Use any open Wi-Fi network without a password
options.C: Keep the default router password unchanged
options.D: Disable Wi-Fi security to improve speed

questions.explanation: Secure Wi-Fi practices include using a trusted network, enabling modern Wi-Fi security such as WPA2 or WPA3, changing default router credentials and keeping router firmware updated.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: Why should users be cautious on public Wi-Fi?

options.A: Untrusted networks may expose users to interception, malicious hotspots or other attacks; sensitive activity should use HTTPS and appropriate security protections
options.B: Public Wi-Fi is always faster than private Wi-Fi
options.C: Public Wi-Fi cannot be used for browsing
options.D: Public Wi-Fi always provides anonymity

questions.explanation: Untrusted networks may expose users to interception, malicious hotspots or other attacks; sensitive activity should use HTTPS and appropriate security protections.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a VPN?

options.A: A Virtual Private Network creates an encrypted tunnel between a device and a VPN endpoint, helping protect traffic on the local network and route it through that endpoint
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) creates an encrypted tunnel between a device and a VPN endpoint, helping protect traffic on the local network and route it through that endpoint.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: Does a VPN guarantee complete anonymity?

options.A: No, a VPN does not eliminate tracking by websites, account-based identification, browser fingerprinting or trust in the VPN provider
options.B: Yes, a VPN guarantees complete anonymity
options.C: Yes, a VPN hides all online activity from everyone
options.D: Yes, a VPN prevents all malware infections

questions.explanation: A VPN does not guarantee complete anonymity; it does not eliminate tracking by websites, account-based identification, browser fingerprinting or trust in the VPN provider.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is spam?

options.A: Unsolicited bulk electronic messages, often sent by email or messaging services
options.B: A type of computer virus
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: Spam is unsolicited bulk electronic messages, often sent by email or messaging services.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a firewall?

options.A: A security system that monitors and controls network traffic according to defined rules
options.B: A type of web browser
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: A firewall is a security system that monitors and controls network traffic according to defined rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: Why should software be updated?

options.A: Updates often fix security vulnerabilities and improve reliability and compatibility
options.B: Updates are only needed to change the software's appearance
options.C: Updates always slow down the computer
options.D: Updates are only needed for games

questions.explanation: Software should be updated because updates often fix security vulnerabilities and improve reliability and compatibility.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a digital certificate?

options.A: An electronic credential used to bind an identity to a public key, typically as part of a public-key infrastructure
options.B: A printed document proving computer ownership
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: A digital certificate is an electronic credential used to bind an identity to a public key, typically as part of a public-key infrastructure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is a digital signature?

options.A: A cryptographic mechanism that can help verify the origin and integrity of a digital message or document
options.B: A handwritten signature scanned into a computer
options.C: A type of web browser
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: A digital signature is a cryptographic mechanism that can help verify the origin and integrity of a digital message or document.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is netiquette?

options.A: The accepted rules of polite, responsible and respectful behaviour when communicating online
options.B: A type of computer network
options.C: A protocol used to transfer files
options.D: A software application for email

questions.explanation: Netiquette is the accepted rules of polite, responsible and respectful behaviour when communicating online.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is copyright infringement on the Internet?

options.A: Using or distributing copyrighted material without permission or a valid legal basis
options.B: Downloading a file from an official website
options.C: Creating a bookmark for a website
options.D: Searching for information on a search engine

questions.explanation: Copyright infringement on the Internet is using or distributing copyrighted material without permission or a valid legal basis.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What should a user do if a website appears fraudulent?

options.A: Do not enter credentials or payment details; close the page, verify the organisation through an independent official channel and report the site where appropriate
options.B: Enter credentials to check if the site works
options.C: Share the website link with friends
options.D: Ignore it and continue browsing

questions.explanation: If a website appears fraudulent, do not enter credentials or payment details; close the page, verify the organisation through an independent official channel and report the site where appropriate.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is the safest way to access a bank website?

options.A: Type the bank's known official address or use its verified official app; avoid links in unexpected messages and check the domain carefully
options.B: Click any link received in an email claiming to be from the bank
options.C: Use a shortened URL sent by an unknown person
options.D: Search for the bank and click the first sponsored result

questions.explanation: The safest way to access a bank website is to type the bank's known official address or use its verified official app; avoid links in unexpected messages and check the domain carefully.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Internet Safety, Privacy and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is the difference between privacy and security online?

options.A: Privacy concerns how personal information is collected and used; security concerns protecting systems and information against unauthorised access or harm
options.B: Privacy and security are exactly the same thing
options.C: Privacy concerns protecting systems; security concerns how information is collected
options.D: Privacy only applies to emails; security only applies to websites

questions.explanation: Privacy concerns how personal information is collected and used; security concerns protecting systems and information against unauthorised access or harm.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Differentiate between the Internet and WWW.

options.A: The Internet is the global network infrastructure; the WWW is a collection of interlinked resources accessed over that infrastructure
options.B: The Internet is a collection of web pages; the WWW is the network infrastructure
options.C: They are exactly the same thing
options.D: The Internet is a browser; the WWW is a search engine

questions.explanation: The Internet is the global network infrastructure; the WWW is a collection of interlinked resources accessed over that infrastructure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Differentiate between a website and a web page.

options.A: A website is a collection of related pages and resources; a web page is one individual document or resource
options.B: A website is one individual document; a web page is a collection of related pages
options.C: They are exactly the same thing
options.D: A website is a browser; a web page is a search engine

questions.explanation: A website is a collection of related pages and resources; a web page is one individual document or resource.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Differentiate between a browser and a search engine.

options.A: A browser is software used to access web content; a search engine is an online service used to find information on the Web
options.B: A browser is an online service; a search engine is software
options.C: They are exactly the same thing
options.D: A browser is a protocol; a search engine is a domain name

questions.explanation: A browser is software used to access web content; a search engine is an online service used to find information on the Web.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Differentiate between a URL and a domain name.

options.A: A domain name identifies a domain; a URL gives the address of a specific resource and may include protocol, domain, path, query and fragment
options.B: A URL identifies a domain; a domain name gives the address of a specific resource
options.C: They are exactly the same thing
options.D: A URL is a protocol; a domain name is a browser

questions.explanation: A domain name identifies a domain; a URL gives the address of a specific resource and may include protocol, domain, path, query and fragment.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Differentiate between HTTP and HTTPS.

options.A: HTTPS protects HTTP communication using TLS; ordinary HTTP does not provide TLS encryption
options.B: HTTP protects HTTPS communication using TLS
options.C: They are exactly the same protocol
options.D: HTTP is used only for email; HTTPS is used only for file transfer

questions.explanation: HTTPS protects HTTP communication using TLS; ordinary HTTP does not provide TLS encryption.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Differentiate between upload and download.

options.A: Upload sends data from a local device to a remote system; download receives data from a remote system to a local device
options.B: Upload receives data from a remote system; download sends data to a remote system
options.C: They are exactly the same process
options.D: Upload only works with images; download only works with documents

questions.explanation: Upload sends data from a local device to a remote system; download receives data from a remote system to a local device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Differentiate between a web server and a web browser.

options.A: A web server provides web resources; a web browser requests, interprets and displays them
options.B: A web server requests web resources; a web browser provides them
options.C: They are exactly the same thing
options.D: A web server is a protocol; a web browser is a domain name

questions.explanation: A web server provides web resources; a web browser requests, interprets and displays them.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Differentiate between a search engine and a web directory.

options.A: A search engine uses automated discovery and ranking systems; a traditional web directory organises selected websites into categories, often through human curation
options.B: A search engine organises websites into categories; a web directory uses automated discovery
options.C: They are exactly the same thing
options.D: A search engine is software; a web directory is a protocol

questions.explanation: A search engine uses automated discovery and ranking systems; a traditional web directory organises selected websites into categories, often through human curation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Which is the standard protocol suite used on the Internet?

options.A: TCP/IP
options.B: HTML
options.C: HTTP only
options.D: FTP only

questions.explanation: TCP/IP is the standard protocol suite used on the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Which protocol is used to resolve domain names to IP addresses?

options.A: DNS
options.B: HTTP
options.C: HTTPS
options.D: FTP

questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) is used to resolve domain names to IP addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Which protocol secures web traffic using TLS?

options.A: HTTPS (HTTP over TLS)
options.B: HTTP
options.C: FTP
options.D: DNS

questions.explanation: HTTPS (HTTP over TLS) secures web traffic using TLS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Which organisation is associated with the invention of the World Wide Web?

options.A: CERN, where Tim Berners-Lee developed the Web
options.B: ARPANET
options.C: W3C
options.D: IETF

questions.explanation: CERN is associated with the invention of the World Wide Web, where Tim Berners-Lee developed the Web.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web?

options.A: Tim Berners-Lee
options.B: Vinton Cerf
options.C: Robert Kahn
options.D: Bill Gates

questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does WWW stand for?

options.A: World Wide Web
options.B: World Wireless Web
options.C: Wide World Web
options.D: Web Wide World

questions.explanation: WWW stands for World Wide Web.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does URL stand for?

options.A: Uniform Resource Locator
options.B: Universal Resource Language
options.C: Uniform Reference Link
options.D: Unified Resource Locator

questions.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does ISP stand for?

options.A: Internet Service Provider
options.B: Internet Security Protocol
options.C: Internal Service Program
options.D: Internet System Platform

questions.explanation: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does DNS stand for?

options.A: Domain Name System
options.B: Digital Network Service
options.C: Data Naming System
options.D: Domain Network Server

questions.explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does HTML stand for?

options.A: HyperText Markup Language
options.B: HyperText Transfer Protocol
options.C: High Text Markup Language
options.D: Hyperlink Text Management Language

questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does HTTP stand for?

options.A: Hypertext Transfer Protocol
options.B: HyperText Markup Language
options.C: High Transfer Text Protocol
options.D: Hyperlink Text Transfer Protocol

questions.explanation: HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does HTTPS stand for?

options.A: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure
options.B: HyperText Markup Language Secure
options.C: High Transfer Text Protocol Standard
options.D: Hyperlink Text Transfer Protocol Secure

questions.explanation: HTTPS stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does TCP stand for?

options.A: Transmission Control Protocol
options.B: Transfer Control Protocol
options.C: Transport Communication Protocol
options.D: Transmission Communication Program

questions.explanation: TCP stands for Transmission Control Protocol.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does IP stand for in TCP/IP?

options.A: Internet Protocol
options.B: Internal Program
options.C: Internet Program
options.D: Information Protocol

questions.explanation: In TCP/IP, IP stands for Internet Protocol.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: What does Wi-Fi refer to?

options.A: A family of wireless networking technologies based on IEEE 802.11 standards; the term is a brand name, not an abbreviation for 'Wireless Fidelity'
options.B: An abbreviation for 'Wireless Fidelity'
options.C: A type of wired network
options.D: A protocol used for email

questions.explanation: Wi-Fi refers to a family of wireless networking technologies based on IEEE 802.11 standards; the term is a brand name, not an abbreviation for 'Wireless Fidelity'.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Which symbol commonly separates the scheme from the rest of a URL?

options.A: A colon followed by two forward slashes for hierarchical URLs, as in https://
options.B: A single forward slash
options.C: A question mark
options.D: A hash symbol

questions.explanation: A colon followed by two forward slashes commonly separates the scheme from the rest of a hierarchical URL, as in https://.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Which symbol introduces the query string in a URL?

options.A: Question mark (?)
options.B: Hash or number sign (#)
options.C: Colon (:)
options.D: Forward slash (/)

questions.explanation: The question mark (?) introduces the query string in a URL.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Which symbol introduces a URL fragment?

options.A: Hash or number sign (#)
options.B: Question mark (?)
options.C: Colon (:)
options.D: Forward slash (/)

questions.explanation: The hash or number sign (#) introduces a URL fragment.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Important Differences and Quick Revision Facts
questions.question: Which URL scheme is commonly used for secure web browsing?

options.A: https
options.B: http
